title: Region Pack 01 Batch 02A — new_sites_needed.json
claim_scope: Supplied site IDs, proposed names, proposed site types, approximate coordinates, and intended nearby-fort relationships only. Not an independent historical source.

title: The Fort of Panhala
claim_scope: Reports a 12th-century Panhala stronghold and the 1191–1192 Bhoja II court/copper-plate tradition. Not evidence of a separate market-town footprint.

title: Panhala Fort
claim_scope: States that the fort dates to the Shilahara period under Bhoja II and that copper plates evidence Panhala under his rule; does not independently attest a distinct market settlement.

title: Tikona Fort, Lonavala — visitor information
claim_scope: Identifies Tikona Peth as the nearest present-day village to Tikona Fort; not evidence of a 1622 settlement.

title: PCA TV: Primary Census Abstract at town, village and ward level, Maharashtra — District Pune, 2011
author: Office of the Registrar General & Census Commissioner, India
claim_scope: Lists Donaje and Gunjavane as present-day Pune district villages. Also lists Malavali under Velhe sub-district; because this may not be the supplied Lohagad-side coordinate, it is used only as a name-collision warning. Not evidence for 1622.

title: Sinhagad
author: District Administration, Pune
claim_scope: Identifies Kondhana as the earlier name of Sinhagad Fort and locates it at present-day village Donaje; not evidence that Donaje was the 1622 village name.

title: Un parler exogène en situation d’endogénéité : le créole portugais de Korlai
author: Robert Chaudenson
claim_scope: States that the village of Korlai was founded around 1595. The date is approximate and the article summarizes earlier historical material.

title: Korlai Village
claim_scope: Notes the older designation Korlai/Kôrlê and its rural character beside Chaul; used for spelling and settlement context, not as a precise 1622 date.

title: Murud-Janjira
publisher: Department of Tourism, Government of Maharashtra
claim_scope: Locates Janjira Fort on an offshore rock near Murud and summarizes its fort history; does not establish when the mainland town of Murud arose.
